scenario: Member's metformin refill rejected; needs new prescriber authorization and has switched pharmacies
text:
CM: Hi, good afternoon, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Renee]] calling from Cadence, am I speaking with [[NAME:Gloria Pruitt]]?
MEMBER: Yes, this is her. Well, this is me. Sorry, I was just laying down for a nap.
CM: Oh, no worries at all. Before we get going I just need to verify, can you give me your date of birth?
MEMBER: Um, [[DOB:June the ninth, nineteen fifty-one]].
CM: Perfect, thank you. And the street address we have on file?
MEMBER: [[ADDRESS:Four oh eight Larkspur Lane]]. Well, it's [[ADDRESS:apartment two B]] but they never put that on anything.
CM: Got it, I'll add that. So I'm calling because I saw the pharmacy flagged your metformin, it looks like the refill didn't go through on the [[DATE:twenty-eighth]].
MEMBER: Yeah, see, that's what I told the girl at the counter. They said doctor, um, doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Halvorsen]] had to sign off again because it's been over a year.
CM: Okay. How do you spell that, just so I get it right?
MEMBER: [[PROVIDER_NAME:H-A-L-V-O-R-S-E-N]]. He's over at the [[FACILITY_NAME:Brookside clinic]].
CM: Okay, and you're still taking the five hundred milligrams twice a day?
MEMBER: Twice a day, with breakfast and with supper.
CM: Okay. I'm gonna send a message to his office [[DATE:today]] and then I'll call the pharmacy. Is that still the CVS on [[ADDRESS:Delmar]]?
MEMBER: No, honey, I switched, I go to the little one by the church now. [[FACILITY_NAME:Hadley Drug]].
CM: [[FACILITY_NAME:Hadley Drug]], okay. Do you have enough pills to get you through the weekend?
MEMBER: I got maybe four left. Maybe five.
CM: Alright, so I'll push on this, and if you don't hear from me by [[DATE:Thursday]] you call me back, okay? My direct line is [[PHONE:three one four, five five five, zero one two two]].
MEMBER: Say that again slower.
CM: Sure. [[PHONE:Three one four... five five five... zero one two two]].
MEMBER: Okay I wrote it on the calendar. Thank you, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Renee]].

scenario: Daughter answers the member's phone after hospital discharge; CM schedules follow-up
text:
CM: Hello, may I speak with [[NAME:Mister Abernathy]], please? This is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Kwame]] with Cadence.
RELATIVE: Um, this is his daughter, he's- hold on, he's in the bathroom. Who did you say?
CM: [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Kwame]], I'm his care manager through his health plan. I'm just checking in since he came home from the hospital.
RELATIVE: Oh. Okay, yeah, he got out [[DATE:Saturday]]. From [[FACILITY_NAME:Mercy West]].
CM: And who am I speaking with?
RELATIVE: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tanya]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tanya Abernathy-Cole]], with a hyphen.
CM: Thanks, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tanya]]. I'm not able to go into details with you until he says it's okay, is he able to come to the phone?
RELATIVE: Dad! Dad, it's the insurance. ... He's coming, he's slow with the walker.
MEMBER: Hello?
CM: Hi, [[NAME:Mister Abernathy]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Kwame]] from Cadence. Can you tell me your date of birth for me?
MEMBER: [[DOB:November second, forty-four]].
CM: Thank you. And is it alright if I talk with your daughter about your care too?
MEMBER: Yeah, yeah, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tanya]] handles all that. Talk to her.
CM: Great. So, um, the discharge papers said you need to see your heart doctor within seven days. Has anybody called you about that?
RELATIVE: No. Nobody. I tried calling doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Okafor]]'s office [[DATE:yesterday]] and it just rang and rang.
CM: [[PROVIDER_NAME:Okafor]], that's [[PROVIDER_NAME:O-K-A-F-O-R]]?
RELATIVE: Yes.
CM: Okay, I have a line to their scheduling. Let me see if I can get him in by [[DATE:the eleventh]]. Does he have a way to get there?
RELATIVE: I work at [[EMPLOYER:Fairview Elementary]] till three so it'd have to be after that, or I can't drive him.
CM: Understood. I'll look for something late afternoon. And he's still weighing himself every morning?
MEMBER: Every morning. One ninety-one [[DATE:today]].
CM: That's good, that's steady. If it goes up three pounds in a day you call the nurse line, okay?
MEMBER: She told me that at the hospital too.
CM: Good. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tanya]], best number for you?
RELATIVE: My cell, [[PHONE:six one four, five five five, zero one eight nine]].
CM: Got it. I'll call you back [[DATE:tomorrow]] with a time.

scenario: Care coordinator books dialysis transport with a ride vendor; schedule and pickup address confirmed
text:
TRANSPORT: [[ORGANIZATION:Lakeshore Medical Rides]], this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Benny]].
CM: Hi [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Benny]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Alicia]] over at Cadence, I've got a standing order I need to set up for dialysis.
TRANSPORT: Sure thing. Member name?
CM: [[NAME:Dorothy Venable]]. [[NAME:V as in Victor, E-N-A-B-L-E]].
TRANSPORT: [[NAME:Venable]]... okay and the member ID?
CM: It's [[MEMBER_ID:M, eight eight two, four zero, seven one six]].
TRANSPORT: [[MEMBER_ID:Eight eight two four zero seven one six]]. Got her. Pickup address?
CM: [[ADDRESS:Thirty-one twelve North Kimball]], it's a two-flat, she's on the first floor. There's a ramp around the side, by the alley.
TRANSPORT: Okay. And where's she going?
CM: [[FACILITY_NAME:Northside Kidney Center]] on [[ADDRESS:Irving Park]].
TRANSPORT: And that's Monday Wednesday Friday?
CM: No, it's Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday. Chair time is six forty-five so she'd need to be picked up like, six, six-fifteen.
TRANSPORT: Saturdays we only have one wheelchair van early. Does she need the wheelchair van?
CM: She uses a walker most days but after treatment she's wiped out, so yeah, I'd say wheelchair to be safe.
TRANSPORT: Okay. Start date?
CM: Can we start [[DATE:this Thursday]]? That's [[DATE:the ninth]].
TRANSPORT: The ninth, yep. Return trip, will-call or scheduled?
CM: Will-call. The center usually calls when she's off the machine, it's about four hours.
TRANSPORT: Got it. Contact number for the member?
CM: Her home is [[PHONE:seven seven three, five five five, zero one three eight]]. Her son [[RELATIVE_NAME:Marcus]] is the backup, I don't have his number on me, sorry.
TRANSPORT: That's fine. Confirmation number is [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:L R, four four nine one]].
CM: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:L R four four nine one]]. Thanks [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Benny]].

scenario: Member refuses to verify identity and the CM cannot discuss details
text:
CM: Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Paulette]] with Cadence care management, I'm trying to reach [[NAME:Raymond Szabo]].
MEMBER: Who's asking?
CM: My name's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Paulette]], I'm a nurse care manager, we work with your health plan. Is this [[NAME:Raymond]]?
MEMBER: How'd you get this number?
CM: It's the number on file with your plan, sir. Before I can talk about anything I just need to confirm your date of birth.
MEMBER: I'm not giving that out over the phone. I got three calls [[DATE:last week]] from people saying they're Medicare.
CM: That's totally fair, and honestly I'm glad you're careful. I can- I can tell you what I'm calling about in general. It's just a check-in after your E R visit.
MEMBER: How do you know I went to the E R?
CM: The plan gets notified when there's a claim. I can't go any further without verifying though.
MEMBER: Then send me a letter.
CM: I can do that. Or if you want, you can call the number on the back of your insurance card and ask for care management, and they'll transfer you to me. That way you know it's real.
MEMBER: What's your name again?
CM: [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Paulette]]. [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Paulette Greer]]. [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:G-R-E-E-R]].
MEMBER: Uh huh.
CM: And you'd ask for extension four one two.
MEMBER: Four twelve. Fine. I'll think about it.
CM: Okay. I'll also mail out a letter [[DATE:this week]]. You have a good afternoon, sir.
MEMBER: Yeah.

scenario: Provider office returns a care manager's voicemail about a missed appointment
text:
CM: Cadence care management, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Jordan]].
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Hi, yes, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Mindy]] from doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Ramaswamy]]'s office at [[FACILITY_NAME:Valley Endocrine]], I'm returning a call about a patient?
CM: Oh, hi, thanks for calling back. Yes, it's about [[NAME:Luis Bermudez]].
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Can you spell the last name?
CM: [[NAME:B-E-R-M-U-D-E-Z]]. Date of birth [[DOB:four, fifteen, seventy-nine]].
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Okay... I've got a [[NAME:Luis Bermudez]] with a [[DOB:April fifteenth]] birthday, yes.
CM: Great. So he told me he had an appointment [[DATE:last Wednesday]] but nobody was there when he showed up? He was pretty upset about it.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Hmm. Let me look. Oh, okay, I see it. So doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Ramaswamy]] was out that day and we moved everybody to the [[FACILITY_NAME:Glendale office]]. We left him a message.
CM: Ah. He might not've gotten it, his voicemail's been full for like a month.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Yeah, that would do it.
CM: Can we get him rebooked? He's on insulin and his A one C was eleven point two at the last draw, so I really don't want him going too long.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Let me see... I have [[DATE:the twenty-first]] at ten-fifteen or [[DATE:the twenty-sixth]] at one-thirty.
CM: Let's do [[DATE:the twenty-first]], ten-fifteen. And that's at your main location, not [[FACILITY_NAME:Glendale]]?
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Main location, [[ADDRESS:nine hundred West Camelback, suite two ten]].
CM: Perfect. And just so I have it, what's his MRN on your side?
PROVIDER_OFFICE: It's [[MRN:V E, zero zero four, seven seven three, one]].
CM: [[MRN:V E zero zero four seven seven three one]]. Thanks so much, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Mindy]].

scenario: Food insecurity screening; member describes running out of groceries and is referred to a pantry
text:
CM: so how have things been, uh, since we last talked
MEMBER: honestly not great. my hours got cut at the [[EMPLOYER:Dollar General]] so
CM: oh I'm sorry to hear that
MEMBER: yeah it's like, I get paid at the start of the month and by like week three there's nothing in the fridge
CM: okay. can I ask you a couple of questions, they're kind of standard ones we ask everybody
MEMBER: sure
CM: in the last twelve months did you ever worry that your food would run out before you got money to buy more
MEMBER: yeah. like every month
CM: okay. and are the kids getting meals at school
MEMBER: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Jaylen]] does, breakfast and lunch. the little one's not in school yet
CM: okay. so there's a couple things I can do. there's a pantry at [[FACILITY_NAME:Greater Hope Baptist]], it's on [[ADDRESS:Cleveland Avenue]] right across from the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:old Sears building]]
MEMBER: oh I know where that is
CM: they're open Tuesdays and Thursdays from like nine to noon. you don't need an appointment
MEMBER: okay
CM: and I'm gonna put in a referral for the produce box program. they deliver. is your address still [[ADDRESS:seventeen oh four Hartford]]
MEMBER: no we moved, um, we're at my mom's now. [[ADDRESS:Twenty-two ninety Marlowe Street]]. [[ADDRESS:Unit C]]
CM: [[ADDRESS:twenty-two ninety Marlowe]], [[ADDRESS:unit C]]. same zip?
MEMBER: no it's [[ZIP:three oh two one five]] now
CM: [[ZIP:three oh two one five]]. got it. and your phone's the same
MEMBER: same phone
CM: okay. and are you still on the WIC for the baby
MEMBER: I let it lapse. I didn't have a ride to the appointment back in [[DATE:August]]
CM: let's get that back too. I'll call you [[DATE:Friday]], is morning okay
MEMBER: after ten. she naps

scenario: Nurse follows up on a fall reported by the home caregiver
text:
RN: Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Bridget]], the nurse from Cadence. We got a message that [[NAME:Mrs. Kowalczyk]] had a fall?
CAREGIVER: Yes, yes. I'm [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Lourdes]], I'm her aide from the agency. She fell [[DATE:Sunday night]], getting up to the bathroom.
RN: Okay. Is she with you now? I'd like to verify with her first.
CAREGIVER: She's right here. [[NAME:Miss Irena]], it's the nurse. Here, here.
MEMBER: Hello, yes?
RN: Hi, [[NAME:Mrs. Kowalczyk]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Bridget]]. Can you tell me your birthday?
MEMBER: [[DOB:The third of February]]. [[DOB:Nineteen thirty... thirty-eight]].
RN: Thank you. How are you feeling? Did you hit your head?
MEMBER: No, no head. My hip. The left. It's purple now.
RN: Ouch. Are you able to put weight on it?
MEMBER: A little. With the cane.
RN: Okay. Can I talk to [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Lourdes]] again for a sec?
CAREGIVER: Yes?
RN: Did anybody take her in to get it looked at?
CAREGIVER: Her son, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Pawel]], he wanted to take her to [[FACILITY_NAME:St. Hedwig's]] but she said no. She don't like the hospital.
RN: Okay. I'm gonna reach out to doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Lindqvist]] and see if they can at least get an X-ray ordered. Is she still on the Eliquis?
CAREGIVER: Yes, the five milligram, two times.
RN: Okay, that's important, because of the bruising. Any rugs in the hallway?
CAREGIVER: There was one. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Pawel]] took it out.
RN: Good. And the nightlight?
CAREGIVER: It burnt out. I will buy one.
RN: Perfect. I'll call back [[DATE:this afternoon]] once I hear from the doctor. Is this the best number, the house phone?
CAREGIVER: Yes, the house. [[PHONE:Four one four, five five five, zero one four one]].

scenario: Care manager calls pharmacy about a prior authorization denial for an inhaler
text:
PHARMACY: [[FACILITY_NAME:Rosedale Pharmacy]], this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Gus]].
CM: Hey [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Gus]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Theresa]] from Cadence again.
PHARMACY: Oh hey [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Theresa]]. Who we got today?
CM: [[NAME:Antoine Lafleur]]. Date of birth [[DOB:twelve, oh-six, sixty-seven]].
PHARMACY: [[NAME:Lafleur]]... [[NAME:L-A-F]]...
CM: [[NAME:L-A, F as in Frank, L-E-U-R]].
PHARMACY: Got him. Trelegy, right? Yeah, that one rejected, it's asking for a PA.
CM: Right, so that's why I'm calling. The prescriber's [[PROVIDER_NAME:Imani Wexler]], she's a nurse practitioner at the [[FACILITY_NAME:Eastgate pulmonary clinic]]. They said they sent the PA on [[DATE:Monday]].
PHARMACY: I don't see an approval yet. What ID are you running him under? I've got two plans on file.
CM: Should be the Medicaid one. [[MEMBER_ID:L A zero zero, uh, nine three, six six one, four]].
PHARMACY: [[MEMBER_ID:Nine three six six one four]]. Okay, yeah, that's the active one. The other one termed [[DATE:in June]].
CM: Okay. In the meantime, does he have any albuterol left?
PHARMACY: We filled albuterol on [[DATE:the second]], two inhalers.
CM: Okay good, so he's not totally without. Can you do an emergency supply on the Trelegy, like a three-day?
PHARMACY: For a brand inhaler, not really, it's one unit. Let me call the help desk and see if they'll do a one-time override.
CM: That'd be amazing. My callback is [[PHONE:five zero four, five five five, zero one one six]], extension two two.
PHARMACY: [[PHONE:Five oh four, five five five, oh one one six]], ext twenty-two. I'll call you before five.

scenario: Behavioral health check-in; member mentions sister and therapist, missed sessions
text:
CM: Hi [[NAME:Devin]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Sam]]. Is now still an okay time?
MEMBER: Yeah. Yeah, I'm on my break.
CM: Cool. So last time we talked you were going to try to get back in with your therapist. How'd that go?
MEMBER: I, um. I went once. [[PROVIDER_NAME:Carla]], the- the counselor at [[FACILITY_NAME:Riverbend Behavioral]]. And then I missed the next two.
CM: Okay. What got in the way?
MEMBER: Work, mostly. They put me on closing at the warehouse. At [[EMPLOYER:Pinnacle Logistics]]. And the sessions are at four.
CM: That's tough. Do they do evenings or telehealth?
MEMBER: She said telehealth on Thursdays maybe. I didn't ask.
CM: Would it help if I called and asked for you?
MEMBER: ...Yeah. Actually yeah.
CM: Okay. On a scale of one to ten, how would you say your mood's been [[DATE:this week]]?
MEMBER: Like a four. It was a two on [[DATE:Saturday]] though. That was a bad day.
CM: I'm glad you're telling me. Any thoughts of hurting yourself on [[DATE:Saturday]] or since?
MEMBER: No. No, not like that. I just stayed in bed. My sister came by. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Keisha]]. She made me eat.
CM: I'm really glad she was there. Are you still taking the sertraline?
MEMBER: Fifty milligrams. Yeah. Most days.
CM: Most days, okay. We can talk about that. I'm going to call [[FACILITY_NAME:Riverbend]] [[DATE:today]] about the Thursday telehealth, and I'll text you after. Still the same number ending in [[PHONE:zero one nine five]]?
MEMBER: Same one.
CM: Okay. And remember, if things get really bad, you can call or text nine eight eight anytime.
MEMBER: I know. Thanks, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Sam]].

scenario: Member calls in to report an address change and new phone number
text:
CM: Thank you for calling Cadence, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Fiona]], how can I help?
MEMBER: Hi, yeah, I need to change my address. I moved.
CM: Sure, I can help with that. Can I get your name?
MEMBER: [[NAME:Marisol Echeverría]].
CM: Okay, and can you spell the last name for me?
MEMBER: [[NAME:E-C-H-E-V-E-R-R-I-A]]. There's an accent on the I but nobody ever puts it.
CM: Got it. And your date of birth?
MEMBER: [[DOB:March thirtieth, nineteen eighty-five]].
CM: And your member ID if you have your card handy?
MEMBER: Um, hold on... okay, it's [[MEMBER_ID:C D N, six, two, zero, four, four... eight, nine, one]].
CM: [[MEMBER_ID:Six two zero four four eight nine one]]. Perfect, I've got you. So what's the new address?
MEMBER: It's [[ADDRESS:five sixty Wentworth Drive]], [[ADDRESS:apartment fourteen]], in [[CITY:Kissimmee]].
CM: [[ADDRESS:Wentworth]], [[ADDRESS:W-E-N-T-W-O-R-T-H]]?
MEMBER: Yes. And the zip is [[ZIP:three four seven four one]]. No wait. [[ZIP:Three four seven four four]]. Sorry. [[ZIP:Four four]].
CM: [[ZIP:Three four seven four four]]. And is the phone number changing too?
MEMBER: Yeah, new phone. [[PHONE:Four oh seven, five five five, zero one zero three]].
CM: Okay. And do you still want your letters in [[LANGUAGE:Spanish]]?
MEMBER: Uh, yes, [[LANGUAGE:Spanish]] for the letters, please. For my mom, she reads them.
CM: No problem. When did you move in?
MEMBER: [[DATE:The first]]. [[DATE:The first of the month]].
CM: Okay, I've updated everything. You'll get a new card in about seven to ten days.

scenario: Insurance ID verification with a member who reads the wrong card; husband corrects
text:
CM: Okay, [[NAME:Mrs. Nakamura]], I just need the member ID off your card, the long number on the front.
MEMBER: Okay, it says... [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:R X, B I N, zero zero four, three three six]]-
CM: Oh, I think that might be the pharmacy BIN, that's- that's a different number. Is there one that says member ID or subscriber ID?
MEMBER: Oh. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ken]]! [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kenji]], which one is it, the insurance one?
RELATIVE: Give it here. Hi, sorry, this is her husband. Okay, member ID is [[MEMBER_ID:W, Q, H, seven four, nine nine, two oh two, one]].
CM: Let me read it back. [[MEMBER_ID:W Q H seven four nine nine two oh two one]]?
RELATIVE: That's it.
CM: Perfect. And, [[NAME:Mrs. Nakamura]], can you confirm your date of birth for me?
MEMBER: [[DOB:August twenty-fifth]]. [[DOB:Nineteen forty-nine]].
CM: Thank you. Okay. And I see a group number that's different from what we had, did either of you change jobs?
RELATIVE: I retired from [[EMPLOYER:Boeing]] [[DATE:end of last year]], so it's the retiree plan now.
CM: Okay, that makes sense. That's probably why the claim from [[FACILITY_NAME:Overlake]] bounced, they had the old group.
MEMBER: The one for my knee?
CM: Yes, the physical therapy from [[DATE:September]]. I'll send them the updated info. Are you still going to PT twice a week?
MEMBER: Mondays and Thursdays. With [[PROVIDER_NAME:Rafael]]. He's very nice but he's very strict.
CM: [[PROVIDER_NAME:Rafael]], okay. Do you know his last name? I don't have him in here.
MEMBER: Something with a D. [[PROVIDER_NAME:Delgado]]? [[PROVIDER_NAME:Del Toro]]? I don't remember.
RELATIVE: [[PROVIDER_NAME:Delgado]].
CM: Thank you. I'll get the claim resubmitted [[DATE:this week]], and I'll mail you a letter confirming the new ID.

scenario: Coordinator schedules a new-patient cardiology appointment for a member
text:

CM: Sure.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: ... Thanks for holding, how can I help?

PROVIDER_OFFICE: Okay, patient's name?
CM: [[NAME:Ruth Ann Delacroix]].
PROVIDER_OFFICE: [[NAME:Delacroix]] like... [[NAME:D-E-L-A]]?

scenario: Short dialysis schedule check; member reports a missed session
text:
RN: Hi [[NAME:Mister Oduya]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Hannah]], the nurse from Cadence. Quick call.
MEMBER: Yes, hello [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Hannah]].
RN: The dialysis center let us know you missed [[DATE:Friday]]. Everything okay?
MEMBER: The van didn't come. I waited outside one hour. Then I went back inside, it was cold.
RN: Oh no. Did you call them?
MEMBER: I called. The lady said they have no record.
RN: Okay, I'll fix that. You're Monday, Wednesday, Friday, right? Same as always?
MEMBER: Monday, Wednesday, Friday. Five thirty in the morning they come.
RN: And you went [[DATE:today]]?
MEMBER: [[DATE:Today]], yes. I am just back. Very tired.
RN: How's your breathing? Any swelling in your legs since missing [[DATE:Friday]]?
MEMBER: A little in the ankles. My weight was up, two point four kilo.
RN: Okay. That's from the missed treatment. Make sure you keep the fluids low like they told you, okay? I'm going to call the ride company right now and make sure [[DATE:Wednesday]] is in there.
MEMBER: Thank you. Thank you very much.

scenario: Three-way call with member, granddaughter, and Cadence nurse about post-stroke medications
text:
CM: Okay, I've got [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Diane]] our nurse on the line too. [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Diane]], you there?
RN: I'm here, hi everybody.
CM: Great. So I've got [[NAME:Mister Featherstone]] and his granddaughter, um, sorry, I didn't catch your name?
RELATIVE: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Brianna]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Bree]]'s fine.
CM: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Bree]], okay.
MEMBER: She's the one with the brains. I just take what she puts in the box.
RN: Ha, well that's the right attitude. So, [[NAME:Mister Featherstone]], they sent you home from [[FACILITY_NAME:Good Samaritan]] on [[DATE:the fifth]], after the stroke, right?
MEMBER: The little stroke. They said little.
RN: The T I A, yeah. And they started you on atorvastatin eighty and clopidogrel, and they stopped the aspirin, is that right, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Bree]]?
RELATIVE: That's what the paper says, but the aspirin's still in the box. I wasn't sure if I should take it out.
RN: Okay, good catch. Let me double-check the discharge list... yes, aspirin is stopped. Go ahead and take it out.
RELATIVE: Okay. And the lisinopril, the paper says ten but the bottle says twenty.
RN: Hmm. Who's the bottle from?
RELATIVE: From doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Mahmoud]], his regular doctor, from before.
RN: Okay, so the hospital lowered it. I want to confirm with doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Mahmoud]] before we change anything, his blood pressure's been running low-ish?
RELATIVE: One oh six over sixty-two [[DATE:yesterday]]. He was dizzy.
RN: Okay, yeah. Hold the twenty, give the ten if you have it from the hospital. I'll call the office [[DATE:this afternoon]].

scenario: Pharmacy calls Cadence about a possible duplicate opioid prescription
text:
CM: Cadence, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ines]].
PHARMACY: Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ravi]], I'm the pharmacist at the Walgreens on [[ADDRESS:Route nine]] in [[CITY:Freehold]]. I'm calling about a shared patient, I got your number off the care plan letter.
CM: Sure. Who's the patient?
PHARMACY: [[NAME:Constance Bianchi]]. [[NAME:B-I-A-N-C-H-I]]. D O B [[DOB:seven, twenty-two, sixty-three]].
CM: Okay, I've got her. What's going on?
PHARMACY: So she's here trying to fill oxycodone five milligram, ninety tablets, from a doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Strand]], but the state monitoring program shows a fill on [[DATE:the twenty-sixth]] from a different prescriber, doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Esposito]], same drug.
CM: Okay. [[PROVIDER_NAME:Esposito]] is her pain management doctor, at [[FACILITY_NAME:Shore Spine and Pain]]. I don't know a [[PROVIDER_NAME:Strand]].
PHARMACY: [[PROVIDER_NAME:Strand]] is with an urgent care, looks like. [[FACILITY_NAME:MedNow]] in [[CITY:Howell]].
CM: Hmm. She did mention she went to urgent care for her back [[DATE:last week]]. Do you know if she told them she has a pain contract?
PHARMACY: She says she didn't know she was supposed to. She's pretty upset.
CM: Okay. Please don't fill it for now. I'm going to call [[FACILITY_NAME:Shore Spine]] and her and sort it out. Can you put a note on her profile?
PHARMACY: Yeah, done. If you need me my direct is [[PHONE:seven three two, five five five, zero one four eight]].
CM: [[PHONE:Seven three two, five five five, zero one four eight]]. Thanks [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ravi]], really appreciate the call.

scenario: Wife calls in on behalf of member with dementia; she is the authorized representative
text:
RELATIVE: Hi, I'm calling about my husband, I'm on his- I'm his authorized whatever. Representative.
CM: Okay, I can help. My name's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Marguerite]]. What's your husband's name?
RELATIVE: [[NAME:Eugene]]. [[NAME:Eugene Pomeroy]]. And I'm [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorraine]].
CM: Thank you, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorraine]]. Can you verify his date of birth and the address?
RELATIVE: [[DOB:May fifth, nineteen forty-one]]. And we're at [[ADDRESS:ninety-two Hollis Road]], [[CITY:Nashua]].
CM: Perfect, and I do see you listed as his representative. What can I do for you?
RELATIVE: Well, he got out of the house [[DATE:Tuesday night]]. Walked all the way down to the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:Mobil station on the corner]]. The police brought him home.
CM: Oh, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorraine]], that must have been so scary.
RELATIVE: I didn't sleep. I can't do this by myself anymore, I just- I'm eighty-three years old.
CM: I hear you. You shouldn't have to. Let's talk about some options. Has his neurologist, um- is it still doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Thibodeaux]]?
RELATIVE: [[PROVIDER_NAME:Thibodeaux]], yes. We saw him back in [[DATE:the spring]].
CM: Okay. So a couple things. There's an adult day program at [[FACILITY_NAME:Maplewood Senior Center]] that takes folks with Alzheimer's, it's weekdays, they have a van. And I can get a home safety evaluation, door alarms, that kind of thing.
RELATIVE: Door alarms. Yes. Our son put a chain on but [[NAME:Gene]] figured it out.
CM: Does your son live nearby?
RELATIVE: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Doug]]'s in [[CITY:Manchester]]. Forty minutes. He works at [[EMPLOYER:Monadnock Paper]], he can't come every day.
CM: Okay. Would you be open to me calling [[RELATIVE_NAME:Doug]] too, so we can all plan together?
RELATIVE: Please. His number is [[PHONE:six oh three, five five five, zero one two seven]].
CM: Got it. I'll call you both [[DATE:Monday]] with the day program info.

scenario: Member mishears care manager's name; quick appointment reminder and transport question
text:
CM: Hi, is this [[NAME:Jacqueline]]?

MEMBER: Oh! Okay, sorry, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Aoife]]. Yeah, hi.

MEMBER: [[ADDRESS:Building six]], yeah. Okay.
CM: And no deodorant that morning, they always say that.
MEMBER: I know, I know. Thanks, hon.

scenario: Hospital case manager calls Cadence about an upcoming discharge and home health needs
text:

CM: Got it. I'll do a call with him and [[RELATIVE_NAME:Leilani]] within forty-eight hours of discharge.

scenario: Member with limited English; son interprets during med reconciliation, interpreter offered
text:

RELATIVE: Hello? Hi, this is her son. She's more comfortable in [[LANGUAGE:Vietnamese]], but I can help, it's fine.
CM: Okay, as long as she's okay with that. Can you ask her if it's okay for you to help, and can she tell me her birthday?
RELATIVE: Hold on, let me ask her. ... She says yes it's okay. Her birthday is [[DOB:the twelfth of October]], [[DOB:nineteen fifty-three]].
CM: Thank you. And your name?
RELATIVE: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Minh Tran]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Minh]], [[RELATIVE_NAME:M-I-N-H]].
CM: Thanks, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Minh]]. Okay, so, can you grab her pill bottles? I want to go through them one by one.
RELATIVE: Okay, okay. First one, amlodipine, five milligram. Once a day.
CM: Okay.
RELATIVE: Then, uh, glipizide, five. Twice a day. And this one... I can't read it, the label's all smudged. It's from the pharmacy in [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:Little Saigon]], the one on [[ADDRESS:Bolsa]].
CM: Is there a prescription number on it?
RELATIVE: Yeah, [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:R X, six one zero, four four, three two]].
CM: Okay, I'll call them on that. Does she take anything else, like herbal stuff, teas?
RELATIVE: She drinks a bitter melon tea. Every day.
CM: Okay, that's good to know, that can lower blood sugar too with the glipizide. Has she had any shaky spells?
RELATIVE: Hang on. ... She says [[DATE:last week]] one time, at church.
CM: Okay. I'm going to let doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Pham]] know. Next time I call, I'll have the interpreter ready so she can talk to me directly too.

scenario: Member with COPD asks about a nebulizer that never arrived; vague address directions
text:
CM: Hey [[NAME:Mister Lyle]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Corey]] from Cadence, how you doing?
MEMBER: Oh, I'm still kickin'. Barely. [cough] Excuse me.
CM: That cough sounds rough. Is that why you called?
MEMBER: Well, partly. That breathing machine, the, uh, the nebulizer? Doctor said it was coming. That was, what, [[DATE:two weeks ago]]. Ain't nothing come.
CM: Okay, let me look. I see an order from doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Bettencourt]], placed on [[DATE:the eighteenth]]. The supplier tried to deliver [[DATE:the twenty-second]] and it says, um, "unable to locate address."
MEMBER: Well, hell. They never can find me. GPS sends 'em to the wrong side of the creek.
CM: Okay, so, help me help them. How would you tell somebody to find you?
MEMBER: You come out [[ADDRESS:County Road eleven]], past the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:Dollar General in Pine Hollow]], and you take the gravel road after the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:Baptist church with the white steeple]]. I'm the third trailer, green, with the dog.
CM: Ha, okay. And the official address is [[ADDRESS:forty-four forty County Road eleven]]?
MEMBER: That's the mailbox. But the mailbox is a mile from the house.
CM: Got it. I'll put all of that in the delivery notes, and I'll give them your cell so the driver can call you. Still [[PHONE:two five six, five five five, zero one zero nine]]?
MEMBER: That's it. Signal's bad though. Tell 'em to call [[RELATIVE_NAME:Darlene]] if they can't get me, she's my sister, lives right up the road.
CM: Do you have [[RELATIVE_NAME:Darlene]]'s number?
MEMBER: Uh, it's... [[PHONE:two five six, five five five, zero one... zero one five... no, zero one five two]]. Yeah, [[PHONE:one five two]].
CM: [[PHONE:Zero one five two]]. Okay. And in the meantime are you using your albuterol inhaler?
MEMBER: Four, five times a day.
CM: Okay, that's a lot. If you're needing it more than every four hours, or you get winded just sitting there, you go to [[FACILITY_NAME:Marshall Medical]], okay? Don't wait on the machine.
MEMBER: Yes ma'am. I mean, yes sir. Sorry.
CM: Ha, it's fine. I'll call you back [[DATE:tomorrow]] with a delivery day.

scenario: Post-partum check-in; member reports headache and elevated blood pressure
text:
RN: Hi, is this [[NAME:Priya]]?
MEMBER: Yes, hi.
RN: Hi [[NAME:Priya]], my name's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Colette]], I'm a nurse with Cadence. Congratulations on the baby!
MEMBER: Thank you. Sorry, she's- she's crying, hold on. Okay.
RN: No, take your time. I just need your date of birth to verify.
MEMBER: [[DOB:Nine, three, ninety-six]].
RN: Thank you. So the baby came [[DATE:on the twenty-seventh]], is that right? At [[FACILITY_NAME:Lakeshore Women's Pavilion]]?
MEMBER: [[DATE:Twenty-seventh]], yes. It was a C-section.
RN: Okay. How are you feeling? How's your incision?
MEMBER: The incision's okay. But I've had this headache since [[DATE:yesterday]]. Like behind my eyes.
RN: Okay. Do you have a blood pressure cuff at home? They usually send one with you.
MEMBER: Yes, they gave me one. I took it an hour ago, it was one fifty-two over ninety-eight.
RN: Okay, [[NAME:Priya]], I want you to listen to me carefully. A headache with a blood pressure that high after delivery can be serious, it can be preeclampsia, even after the baby's born. I want you to go to labor and delivery triage now, not [[DATE:tomorrow]].
MEMBER: Now? I... my husband's at work.
RN: Is there anyone who can drive you? Or I can help you get a ride.
MEMBER: My mother-in-law is here. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Mrs. Raghunathan]], she can watch the baby, but she doesn't drive.
RN: Okay. Can you call your husband?
MEMBER: Yes. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Arjun]] works at [[EMPLOYER:Kessler and Vance]], downtown, it's like twenty minutes.
RN: Okay. If he can't get there in twenty minutes, call nine one one, okay? Any vision changes, chest pain, trouble breathing, call nine one one right away.
MEMBER: Okay. Okay. I'm calling him.
RN: I'm going to call the triage desk and let them know you're coming. I'll check on you [[DATE:tonight]].

scenario: CM conferences member into a call with a PCP office to book a physical; NPI requested for referral
text:
CM: Okay [[NAME:Mister Haddad]], I've got the office on the line. Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Lauren]] from Cadence, I've also got the patient on with me.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Hi, okay, this is [[FACILITY_NAME:Cedar Park Family Medicine]], you're talking to [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Bea]].
CM: Hi [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Bea]]. We need to book his annual physical, and also, um, I need doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Whitcombe]]'s NPI for a referral form.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Sure. Patient, can you give me your name and date of birth?
MEMBER: [[NAME:Haddad]], [[NAME:Nabil]]. [[DOB:Sixth of July]], [[DOB:sixty-two]].
PROVIDER_OFFICE: [[NAME:Nabil]]... [[NAME:Haddad]], two Ds?
MEMBER: One D in the middle, two at the... no. [[NAME:H-A-D-D-A-D]]. Two in the middle.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Got you. Okay, the physical. Doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Whitcombe]] has [[DATE:December ninth]] at eight a m, fasting.
MEMBER: [[DATE:December]]? That's far.
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Physicals are booking out about two months. I can put you on the wait list.
MEMBER: Fine, [[DATE:December ninth]], and the wait list.
CM: And the NPI?
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Hold on... it's [[NPI:one, three, eight, two, zero, five, seven, seven, four, one]].
CM: [[NPI:One three eight two, zero five seven, seven four one]].
PROVIDER_OFFICE: Yep.
CM: Thank you. [[NAME:Mister Haddad]], you got the date written down?
MEMBER: My wife's writing it. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Samira]], [[DATE:December ninth]], eight o'clock, no eating.

scenario: Member upset about a bill; CM explains it's from an out-of-network lab and gives the claim number
text:
MEMBER: -and I am not paying four hundred dollars for a blood test, I'm sorry.
CM: I totally understand, [[NAME:Ms. Greenleaf]]. Let's figure out what happened. Do you have the bill in front of you?
MEMBER: I do. It's from [[ORGANIZATION:Quantis Diagnostics]]. I've never heard of them.
CM: Okay, and what's the date of service on there?
MEMBER: [[DATE:August fourteenth]].
CM: Okay, and is there an account number on the top right?
MEMBER: Account... [[ACCOUNT_ID:Q D, seven seven zero, one one four, five, eight]].
CM: [[ACCOUNT_ID:Seven seven zero one one four five eight]], okay. So, what probably happened is your doctor's office drew the blood but sent it to an outside lab, and that lab isn't in your network.
MEMBER: Nobody told me that! I went to doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Castellanos]] like I always do.
CM: I know, it's frustrating, and honestly this happens a lot. The good news is there's a process for this. I'm going to open a, um, a billing review. Your reference number for that is [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:B R, two zero two six, dash, zero four four one nine]].
MEMBER: Hold on, I need a pen. Okay.
CM: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:B R, two zero two six, dash, zero four four one nine]].
MEMBER: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:Two zero two six... zero four four one nine]].
CM: You got it. And don't pay it while it's under review. If they call you, give them that number.
MEMBER: Okay. Thank you. Sorry I yelled.
CM: Oh, you didn't yell. Honestly, I'd be mad too.

scenario: Ride no-show; CM calls transport vendor while member waits outside the clinic
text:

TRANSPORT: [[ORGANIZATION:MetroAccess Partners]] dispatch, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Yolanda]].
CM: Hi [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Yolanda]], this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Nico]] with Cadence. I've got a member who's been waiting for a return trip for an hour and a half at [[FACILITY_NAME:Fulton Street Medical Plaza]].
TRANSPORT: Name?
CM: [[NAME:Francesca Lombardo]].
TRANSPORT: [[NAME:Lom]]... can you spell it?
CM: [[NAME:L-O-M-B-A-R-D-O]].
TRANSPORT: Hm. I have a [[NAME:Lombardi]] with an I?
CM: No, with an O at the end. Trip number should be [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:seven seven, four oh, two two]].
TRANSPORT: Oh, okay, here it is. It was marked a no-show at two-ten.

TRANSPORT: Ah. Driver went to [[ADDRESS:Hoyt]]. Okay, I'm sending a car. Twenty, twenty-five minutes.

scenario: Brief outreach call; member is at work and asks to be called back
text:
CM: Hi, may I speak to [[NAME:Tobias Engel]]?
MEMBER: This is [[NAME:Toby]]. Who's this?

scenario: Caller claims to be the member's nephew but isn't on the authorization; CM gives only general info
text:
RELATIVE: Yeah, hi, I'm calling for my uncle, [[NAME:Vernon Tibbs]]. I need to know when his next appointment is.
CM: Hi, thanks for calling. My name's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Esther]]. Can I get your name?
RELATIVE: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Curtis]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Curtis Tibbs]].
CM: Okay, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Curtis]]. Let me check if you're listed on his account... I'm sorry, I don't see you as an authorized contact. I've got a [[RELATIVE_NAME:Jolene]] listed.
RELATIVE: That's my mom. She's in the hospital herself right now, at [[FACILITY_NAME:Baptist East]]. That's the whole problem, she's the one who does all his stuff.
CM: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. I hope she's okay.
RELATIVE: She'll be okay. But he can't remember anything, I need to know when to take him.
CM: I understand. I can't give out details without his permission, but if he's there with you, he can tell me it's okay over the phone and I can add you.
RELATIVE: He's- yeah, he's here. Uncle [[NAME:Vern]]. Uncle [[NAME:Vern]], come here. Talk to the lady.
CM: ...
RELATIVE: He's saying he don't want to talk on the phone. He's stubborn.
CM: That's okay. What I can do is, I'll call his doctor's office and ask them to call his number directly with the appointment reminder. And I'll send him the authorization form in the mail so he can add you.
RELATIVE: Mail it where?
CM: To the address on file.
RELATIVE: He's at my place now, on [[ADDRESS:Shelbyville Road]], near the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:Oxmoor mall]].
CM: I'd need him to update that himself, unfortunately. I know it's a lot of hoops.
RELATIVE: Yeah. Alright. Whatever. Thanks.

scenario: Diabetic foot wound check; daughter-in-law answers and helps, podiatry appointment set
text:

RN: Hi, good morning, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Matthew]], a nurse with Cadence. Is [[NAME:Mister Okonjo]] available?
RELATIVE: Which one? There's two of them here. [laughs] You mean [[NAME:Papa]], the older one? [[NAME:Chukwuemeka]]?
RN: Yes, [[NAME:Chukwuemeka]], uh, I hope I'm saying that right.
RELATIVE: You're close! It's [[NAME:Chukwuemeka]]. Most people call him [[NAME:Emeka]]. I'm his daughter-in-law, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ngozi]]. Hold on.
MEMBER: Hello. This is [[NAME:Emeka]].
RN: Good morning sir. Before we start, can you tell me your date of birth?
MEMBER: [[DOB:The first of January]], [[DOB:nineteen fifty]]. Easy to remember.
RN: Very easy. Thank you. So I'm calling about the sore on your foot. The wound clinic said you missed the visit on [[DATE:the thirtieth]].
MEMBER: My son was traveling. Nobody to drive.
RN: Okay. How does the foot look [[DATE:today]]? Any redness going up the leg, or smell, or fever?
MEMBER: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ngozi]] looks at it every day. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ngozi]]!
RELATIVE: It's about the size of a nickel, on the ball of his right foot. There's a little yellow but no smell. No fever, I check every night.
RN: That's really helpful, thank you. And his sugars?
RELATIVE: Morning ones are like one-sixty, one-seventy.
RN: Okay. I'd like to get him back in [[DATE:this week]]. The podiatrist at [[FACILITY_NAME:Lakeview Wound Care]] is doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Ferreira-Doyle]], and they have Friday mornings open. Can you do [[DATE:this Friday]]?
RELATIVE: [[DATE:Friday]] I can drive him. I'm off work.
RN: Great. I'll book it and call you back with the time. What's the best number, this one?
RELATIVE: This is the house. Use my cell, [[PHONE:two one four, five five five, zero one three oh]].
RN: [[PHONE:Two one four, five five five, zero one three zero]]?
RELATIVE: Yes, sorry, zero.
RN: Got it. And keep him off that foot as much as you can, okay?
MEMBER: She doesn't let me walk anywhere. She's worse than the doctor.
